nodes.description: Transgenic mice expressing the founder allele in osteoblasts under the 2.3 kb Col1a1 promoter. Femora show markedly increased trabecular bone volume and density, with reduced osteoclast differentiation and number, lower serum TRACP 5b and CTX, and higher serum IFN-gamma.
Kinky or curly hair present at birth in about 85% of affected people; it is retained after infancy in about half and may straighten by adolescence.

evidence.reference_title: DLX3 homeodomain mutations cause tricho-dento-osseous syndrome with novel phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: After mutational analysis of DLX3, we identified 2 missense mutations affecting the conserved homeodomain. We suggest that TDO is essentially caused by loss of function and haploinsufficiency of DLX3.

nodes.description: DLX3 is a homeodomain transcription factor required for terminal differentiation programs in tooth, bone, hair and epidermis. The founder c.571_574delGGGG protein reaches the nucleus but cannot bind the canonical DLX3 element, has defective transactivation and lowers the activity of co-expressed wild-type DLX3, a dominant-negative effect. Homeodomain missense, splice-site and whole-gene-deletion alleles instead indicate loss of function and haploinsufficiency. The molecular lesion is therefore reduced DLX3-dependent transcription, reached by different routes for different alleles.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular consequences of a frameshifted DLX3 mutant leading to Tricho-Dento-Osseous syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Immunocytochemical analysis revealed that both DLX3(WT) and DLX3(TDO) recombinant proteins are targeted to the nucleus. However, as demonstrated by electrophoresis mobility shift assay, DLX3(TDO) is not able to bind to the canonical Dlx3 binding site.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular consequences of a frameshifted DLX3 mutant leading to Tricho-Dento-Osseous syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Moreover, the transcriptional activity of DLX3(WT) is significantly reduced in the presence of the mutated isoform, indicating that DLX3(TDO) has a dominant negative effect on DLX3(WT) transcriptional activity.

evidence.reference_title: DLX3 c.561_562delCT mutation causes attenuated phenotype of tricho-dento-osseous syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Careful phenotyping of individuals with allelic DLX3 mutations reveals marked differences in phenotypic severity indicating that the carboxy-terminus of the DLX3 protein is critical in determining its function during development in these different tissues.

nodes.description: TDO alleles delay senescence of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and pre-osteoblasts, extending their functional lifespan. This is proposed to reconcile reduced per-cell osteogenic potential with the high bone mass of TDO.

evidence.reference_title: Senescence: novel insight into DLX3 mutations leading to enhanced bone formation in Tricho-Dento-Osseous syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Both DLX3 mutations (c.533 A>G and c.571_574delGGGG) delayed cellular senescence when they were introduced into pre-osteoblastic cells MC3T3-E1.

nodes.description: DLX3 activates odontoblastic genes in dental pulp cells, including WNT10A through a conserved enhancer. Reduced DLX3 function is proposed to disturb odontoblast differentiation and dentin formation, giving thin dentin and the enlarged pulp chambers of taurodontism. The evidence is human genetic and cell based; it is strongest for alleles with a mesenchymal-dominant dental phenotype.

This is not a uniform property of TDO alleles: Q178R patient-derived stromal cells show reduced osteogenic potential, and founder-allele transgenic mice show no increase in dynamic bone formation in vivo.

nodes.description: Abnormal hair-follicle differentiation is the presumed basis of the congenital kinky hair, by analogy with the follicular dysplasia found in a DLX3-mutant calf. In human TDO, scanning electron microscopy of hair shafts has not shown a consistent ultrastructural abnormality, and why the hair often straightens after infancy is unexplained.

In transgenic mice expressing the founder allele in osteoblasts, osteoclast differentiation, osteoclast number and serum resorption markers fall while serum IFN-gamma rises, and trabecular bone volume and density increase without an increase in dynamic bone formation rate. In RAW 264.7 cells, wild-type and Q178R DLX3 suppress osteoclastogenesis through microRNA-124 and NFATc1.

nodes.description: Recurrent 4-bp deletion causing a frameshift that replaces the C-terminal region downstream of the homeodomain. Shared, with a common surrounding haplotype, by the North Carolina and Virginia kindreds in which TDO was first characterized, indicating descent from a common ancestor. The mutant protein acts as a dominant negative.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a mutation in DLX3 associated with tricho-dento-osseous (TDO) syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: A common DLX3 gene mutation is responsible for tricho-dento-osseous syndrome in Virginia and North Carolina families.
evidence.snippet: These findings suggest that all people with TDO who have been evaluated have inherited the same DLX3 gene deletion mutation from a common ancestor.

nodes.description: Three alleles reported in UK families ascertained through amelogenesis imperfecta. All gave amelogenesis imperfecta and taurodontism with attenuated systemic TDO features. The whole-gene deletion is the clearest evidence that DLX3 haploinsufficiency alone is pathogenic.
